correctness.summary: For flat signed spectra the cumulants and cumulant generating function are explicit. Series inversion gives the stated cubic and quartic rate-function terms; a conjugate-measure moderate-deviation calculation transfers them to the extreme Gaussian scale, and independence gives the shifted Gumbel law. The canonical log-cubic and log-quadratic regimes follow directly, as does the same-effective-rank separation. Standalone symbolic and exact-distribution calculations support the algebra and critical shifts.

limitations: The sharp theorem treats independent coordinates and flat spectra of common absolute eigenvalue.
General spectra and cross-coordinate dependence may require additional cumulants or other spectral information.
The two-term crossover assumes R/(log p)^(5/3) tends to infinity; lower ranks may require higher Cramér-series terms.
The result concerns the chaos-to-Gaussian step rather than the separate finite-sample U-statistic-to-chaos approximation.
The full theorem text of Anderson–Coles–Hüsler (1997) was not inspected and remains an originality uncertainty.
Independent audit has not been performed.

originality.scope: to the best of our knowledge
originality.summary: Cai–Hu 2026 already gives a general sufficient fourth-effective-rank condition, and classical Cramér/Petrov theory plus Bose–Dasgupta–Maulik 2008 cover important moderate-deviation and positive-gamma ingredients. The claim is restricted to the explicit signed-flat two-term phase diagram, exact critical Kolmogorov profile, log-cubic versus log-quadratic sign-balance split, and the same-r4 same-fourth-cumulant indefinite spectra with opposite Gaussianization limits. Searches did not locate these statements. The full theorem text of Anderson–Coles–Hüsler 1997 was not inspected, so its generic triangular-array Cramér theory remains a concrete residual risk.

review_statement: Same-model review: passed. Independent audit: not yet performed.

value.summary: The result identifies a missing spectral coordinate in a new high-dimensional chaos phase theorem: a third signed spectral moment can change the sharp effective-rank scale by a full power of log p. The explicit same-effective-rank construction proves that fourth effective rank is useful as a sufficient control but cannot alone be a sharp phase coordinate across signed spectra.
